steps.title: Anomalies
steps.text:
This scenario features four group resources—Panic, Fracture, Beast, and Support—collectively known as anomalies. Panic, Fracture, and Beast represent the effects of the spreading portals, and are usually negative. Support represents the efforts of your fellow investigators and is positive.
Anomalies are recorded on the Anomaly Tracker card. When an effect tells you to gain 1 or more anomalies, place that many resource tokens in the corresponding section. When an effect asks you to spend or remove anomalies, remove that many resource tokens

steps.title: Left and Right
steps.text: If you are playing in Epic Multiplayer Mode, the event organizer will designate two other groups as your "left" and "right." (If you are playing with a total of two groups, the other group will be both your left and your right.) When an effect tells another group to gain an anomaly, pass that instruction to the corresponding group. If you are playing in Single Group Mode, whenever an effect tells you to give an instruction to another group, perform that instruction yourself. For example, if told that the group to your left gains 1 Panic, instead gain 1 Panic yourself.

steps.title: Clockwise and Anticlockwise
steps.text: In this scenario, locations are placed in a circle. Some effects will instruct you to move clockwise or anticlockwise, which simply means to move to the location immediately in the clockwise (or anticlockwise) direction from your current location. Note that these effects do not require location connections—an effect can still make you move clockwise even if a card effect has stopped your destination from being connected to your location.

steps.title: The Turning Gear Key
steps.text: For the purposes of this scenario, The Turning Gear key is only used as a marker for tokens and an objective for investigators to obtain. Treat The Turning Gear’s text box as if it were blank for the duration of this scenario. The full rules for keys are therefore not required to play this scenario; however, if the investigators are playing this scenario as part of The Scarlet Keys campaign, they may be able to earn The Turning Gear and use it in future scenarios.

steps.title: Linked Cards
steps.text: This scenario features connected pairs of [[Part 1]] and [[Part 2]] story cards. Each [[Part 1]] story card has the Linked keyword, specifying which [[Part 2]] it connects to. The act will instruct you what to do with the linked [[Part 2]] cards when [[Part 1]] cards come into play.

steps.title: Concealed X
steps.text: Concealed X is a keyword that first appeared in The Scarlet Keys campaign. Concealed enemies represent hidden enemies whose true location is a mystery until the investigators work to expose where—and in some cases, who—they truly are. When a scenario includes one or more concealed enemies, investigators are instructed to set aside several concealed mini-cards. These mini-cards are double-sided. The facedown side represents the possible location of a concealed enemy. The revealed side reveals the mini-card’s true nature—an enemy’s true location, or simply a decoy.

When an investigator draws an enemy with the concealed X keyword (or is instructed to resolve an enemy’s concealed keyword), they spawn that enemy into a game area above the agenda deck, not at any location. This area is called “the shadows,” and represents enemies the investigators know exist somewhere on the map, but are unsure where. Then, that investigator takes the set-aside concealed mini-card that matches that enemy, along with X decoys (where X is defined by that enemy’s concealed X value), shuffles them facedown, and puts them into play distributed as evenly as possible among each location in play, starting with the locations nearest to them. Then, at each of those locations that already had 1 or more concealed mini-cards, they shuffle each of them facedown as well. For example: Amina draws Coterie Agent (A), which has “concealed 2.” She first spawns the Coterie Agent into the shadows. Then, she takes the set-aside Coterie Agent (A) mini-card, along with 2 decoys, shuffles them facedown, and places one at each of the three locations nearest to her. Then, if any of those locations already had 1 or more concealed mini-cards, she would shuffle each concealed mini-card at those locations, as well.
Enemies in the shadows observe the following additional rules:

bullets.text: Enemies in the shadows are considered to be in play, but not at any particular location. They cannot move until they leave the shadows.
Enemies in the shadows can qualify as the “nearest” enemy, but only if there are no other enemies in play at any location.
Enemies in the shadows cannot be damaged or leave play via player card effects.

steps.title: Concealed Mini-Cards
steps.text: While in play, concealed mini-cards represent the possible location of an enemy in the shadows. In order to deal with such an enemy, its true location must first be discovered by exposing its mini-card. This can be done via one of three methods: fighting, evading, or investigating.

Concealed mini-cards are not enemies and cannot be engaged like enemies. However, any investigator at the same location as a concealed mini-card may attempt to expose it by successfully attacking it or evading it (as if it were an engaged enemy), or by successfully investigating its location. The difficulty to successfully attack or evade a concealed mini-card is equal to the shroud value of its location.

bullets.text: An investigator may also use a card effect that automatically evades an enemy, deals damage to an enemy, or discovers a clue at a location in order to instead expose a concealed mini-card.

steps.text: If an investigator chooses to expose a concealed mini-card, that effect replaces the standard effects of the action or ability that exposed it. (i.e., if an enemy’s mini-card is exposed by evasion or damage, the matching enemy is not evaded, nor does it take damage. If a mini-card is exposed by discovering clues or investigating, no clues are discovered.)
If a concealed mini-card is exposed (via any of the above methods), flip it to its revealed side.

bullets.text: If it is a decoy, set it aside, out of play, with no effect.

If it is an enemy’s mini-card, that enemy is now exposed. Place the matching enemy in the shadows at that mini-card’s location, then set that mini-card aside, out of play. (That enemy is no longer in the shadows, and is now at the location where its mini-card was located). Then, if there are no other enemies in the shadows, set all remaining concealed mini-cards in play aside, out of play.

steps.text: Only one concealed mini-card may be exposed per effect unless explicitly stated. (i.e., an effect that deals 3 damage to each enemy at a location does not expose all concealed mini-cards at that location; only one.)

steps.title: Elusive
steps.text:
Elusive enemies represent enemies who want to avoid the investigators for their own survival or to accomplish their own goals.
If a ready enemy with the elusive keyword attacks or is attacked, after that attack resolves, that enemy immediately disengages from all investigators, moves to a connecting location (with no investigators, if able), and exhausts. This effect occurs whether the enemy was engaged with the attacking investigator or not.
If you are playing The Turning Gear as a side-story while playing The Scarlet Keys campaign:

The Turning Gear is something of a legend, even by the standards of paradimensional artefacts. The Foundation's records have reports of encounters in Birmingham, Taipei, and Constantinople, but no concrete information on its whereabouts. With no leads and plenty of other avenues to pursue, you are content with never finding this elusive relic.
It, on the other hand, wants to find you.
The signs are subtle at first — a flock of birds not native to this continent, a woman babbling at a crowd in a language none of them speaks — but it isn't long before you spot the first portal. Shimmering and opalescent, it hangs in the air before you in open defiance of all physical laws.
There was probably once a time when you wouldn't have stepped through a strange portal, but that was then and this is now.
You find yourself on an arid plain. The African savannah, perhaps? A few minutes of exploring turn up nothing of interest save for another portal, much the same as the first. Eager to escape the heat, you pass through it, this time finding yourself in a bustling city. Somewhere in China, judging by the signage.
You step through portal after portal, travelling the globe in minutes. Shortly, you find yourself outside the Tower of London, surrounded by figures in suits darting to and fro. The Foundation?
Your suspicions are confirmed when Commissioner Taylor corners you. "Ah, capital, you're here. As you may have gathered, we have a crisis on our hands."

Fifteen minutes of cautious investigation have taught you very little. The anomaly simply hangs in the air, vaguely circular, opaque, swirling gently. It looks like some kind of portal, and certainly objects can be pushed into it and then pulled out, unharmed. You have spent fifteen minutes trying to avoid stepping into it, but you are rapidly running out of other avenues of approach.
A single piece of information tickles at your brain — an artefact, mentioned by an academic colleague. "The Turning Gear," an object capable of opening gates in spacetime. Could this be related?
Feeling nervous and underprepared, you step through the portal.
You find yourself on an arid plain. The African savannah, perhaps? A few minutes of exploring turn up nothing of interest save for another portal, much the same as the first. Eager to escape the heat, you pass through it, this time finding yourself in a bustling city.Somewhere in China, judging by the signage.
You step through portal after portal, travelling the globe in minutes. Shortly, you find yourself outside the Tower of London, surrounded by figures in suits darting to and fro. Before you can do much of anything, you are spotted by a woman in a black suit, who cuts through the crowd towards you, hand on her weapon.
"You don't look like Coterie agents."
You try to explain who you are, but after a few seconds she cuts you off. "Okay, fine. A bunch of amateurs in the wrong place. Go home, let the professionals handle this."
 You object — you have some experience with the supernatural, and you can hardly just turn around and go home. The woman's mouth twitches with irritation. "Fine. Consider yourself deputized. I am Commissioner Taylor, and I guess you're working for me now."

You ask about the choice of location. "There's a lot more portal activity here than elsewhere — the working theory is it's drawn to prior paradimensional activity. That and a lack of resources — this sorry lot are all I could pull together on short notice.
"See what you can figure out, check in regularly, and avoid burning, freezing, drowning, and so on. I can't afford to lose any personnel at the moment — not even you."

You ask about the choice of location. "There's a lot more portal activity here than elsewhere — the working theory is it's drawn to prior paradimensional activity. In any case, this is an ideal place to coordinate our agents in the field.
"Yes, we have other assets working on this. Don't look so surprised; it's a global problem. Try to coordinate with other teams — heaven knows we'll need any advantage we can get.

Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: Flood, Military Maneuvers, Red Guard, and Unbound Dimensions. Set these encounter sets aside, out of play, along with each [[Part 1]] and [[Part 2]] card, the Support card, The Turning Gear key, and The Turning Gear asset.
Put each [[City]] location into play, [[Turmoil]] side up. Each investigator begins in London.
Put the Anomaly Tracker into play next to the scenario reference card.

Gather each decoy mini-card and each of the following mini-cards: Coterie Operative, Coterie Shadowguard, Coterie Spy, Coterie Stalker, Coterie Trickster, and Coterie Troublemaker. Set them aside, out of play.
Shuffle the remaining encounter cards to build the encounter deck.

Remember that effects which move investigators, enemies, etc. clockwise or anticlockwise do not require location connections — an effect can still make you move clockwise even if a card effect has stopped your destination from being connected to your location.
Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.

resolutions.title: Resolution 1
resolutions.text: Another key in hand, safe from the Coterie and the world safe from its effects. As an added bonus, you’re able to exert some control over its portals as it powers down, granting you an expedited route to your next destination

resolutions.title: Resolution 2
resolutions.text: With the Gear in hand, you are able to navigate back to where you started through the network of closing portals. The world may be safe from the Gear (for now), but other threats are still out there. At least you now have one more tool for dealing with them.

resolutions.title: Resolution 3
resolutions.text:
As the portals begin to close all around you, it is all you can do to reach your starting point and resume your search, hoping all the while that the Gear is in safe hands.
You receive a telegram a few days later. Another group, working for the Foundation, took control of the Gear on their behalf. You're not sure how much you can trust these strangers, but at least it doesn't lie with the more unsavory elements of the Coterie.

resolutions.title: Resolution 4
resolutions.text:
As the portals begin to close all around you, it is all you can do to reach your starting point and resume your search, hoping all the while that the Gear is in safe hands.
Alas, it is not. Days later, you begin to witness its spatial warping effect acting on behalf of your adversaries.
